More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

The Nepal Flash Floods-triggered by extreme monsoon downpours and glacial collapse near the Himalayas-unleashed millions of tons of water and debris across rivers like the Bagmati and Trishuli. Nestled in the high Himalayas, Nepal remains exceptionally vulnerable to Climate Change and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). When relentless rainfall causes mountain rivers to overflow, massive torrents of mud and water wash over the Kathmandu Valley and surrounding mountain districts, submerging highways, destroying critical hydropower infrastructure, and cutting off entire communities. With disaster management authorities (NDRRMA) and global relief agencies mobilizing massive search-and- rescue operations, these flash floods serve as a stark warning about the rising environmental threats facing Himalayan communities and global climate stability. #nepalfloods #nepal #climatechange #emotional #flashflood

During the rescue operation, a soldier heard voices coming from inside the tunnel and asked, “How many people are there?” He then reassured those trapped inside, saying, “Don’t panic, don’t panic. We’re coming. The Nepal Army is coming. Stay calm and don’t be afraid. We are already very close to you.” Following the floods, Nepal Army personnel and technical rescue teams have been deployed to search for and rescue people believed to be trapped inside tunnels at various hydropower projects in Rasuwa.
